```{=html}
<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
  let slideIndex = 0;
  const slides = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(".hero-slide"));
  const credit = document.querySelector(".hero-credit");

  const credits = [
    "Credit: BSF team",
    "Credit: BSF team A",
    "Credit: BSF teamB",
    "Credit: BSF team C",
    "Credit: ? (image DSCN3267)",
    "Credit: Prakash Basnet"
  ];

  // Randomize image order
  const order = slides.map((_, i) => i);

  for (let i = order.length - 1; i > 0; i--) {
    const j = Math.floor(Math.random() * (i + 1));
    [order[i], order[j]] = [order[j], order[i]];
  }

  function showSlide(position) {
    const imageIndex = order[position];

    // Change the image using your existing fade effect
    slides.forEach(slide => slide.classList.remove("active"));
    slides[imageIndex].classList.add("active");

    // Fade the credit out first
    credit.classList.remove("active");

    // Wait for the credit's fade-out before changing its text
    setTimeout(() => {
      credit.textContent = credits[imageIndex];

      // Allow the browser to apply opacity: 0 before fading in
      void credit.offsetWidth;
      credit.classList.add("active");
    }, 1500);
  }

  // Show the first randomized slide
  showSlide(slideIndex);

  // Change slides every 5 seconds
  if (slides.length > 1) {
    setInterval(() => {
      slideIndex = (slideIndex + 1) % slides.length;
      showSlide(slideIndex);
    }, 5000);
  }
});
</script>
```

<h2>Black Soldier Fly microfarms in Madagascar</h2>

<p>This project developed research, guides and training for local farmers to use soldier fly farming (BSF) as a simple and low-cost way to turn waste and invasive plants into valuable resources like animal feed, organic fertilizer and nutritious food.</p>

<p>**Project leader:** Dr Brian Fisher</p>

<p>**Project website:** [Madagascar Bio](https://www.madagascarbio.org/bsf-farms.html)</p>

<p>Image credit: The BSF team (?)</p>

:::

<h2>Gharial conservation in Nepal</h2>

<p>The Himalayan Gharial Project is a conservation and research initiative dedicated to understanding why the gharials remain Critically Endangered in Nepal, and how to support their long-term recovery.</p>

<p>**Project leader:** Dr Phoebe Griffith</p>

<p>**Project website:** [Himalayan Nature](https://www.himalayannature.org/works/projects/himalayan-gharial-project/)</p>
<p>Image credit: The Himalayan Gharial team (?)</p>
